id: Practice Direction 34A – Depositions And Court Attendance By Witnesses
content:
# PRACTICE DIRECTION 34A – DEPOSITIONS AND COURT ATTENDANCE BY WITNESSES

# This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34] Contents of this Practice Direction

## WITNESS SUMMONSES

## Issue of witness summons

## 1.1 A witness summons may require a witness to:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1 A witness summons may require a witness to:] (1) attend court to give evidence,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1 A witness summons may require a witness to:] (2) produce documents to the court, or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1 A witness summons may require a witness to:] (3) both,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1 A witness summons may require a witness to:] on either a date fixed for the hearing or such date as the court may direct 1 .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1 A witness summons may require a witness to:] 1.2 Two copies of the witness summons 2 should be filed with the court for sealing, one of which will be retained on the court file.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1 A witness summons may require a witness to:] 1.3 A mistake in the name or address of a person named in a witness summons may be corrected if the summons has not been served.

## 1.4 The corrected summons must be re-sealed by the court and marked ‘Amended and Re-Sealed’.

## Witness summons issued in aid of an inferior court or tribunal

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Witness summons issued in aid of an inferior court or tribunal] 2.1 A witness summons may be issued in the High Court or the County Court in aid of a court or tribunal which does not have the power to issue a witness summons in relation to the proceedings before it 3 .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Witness summons issued in aid of an inferior court or tribunal] 2.2 A witness summons referred to in paragraph 2.1 may be set aside by the court which issued it 4 .

## 2.3 An application to set aside a witness summons referred to in paragraph 2.1 will be heard:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 2.3 An application to set aside a witness summons referred to in paragraph 2.1 will be heard:] (1) in the High Court by a Master at the Royal Courts of Justice or by a District Judge in a District Registry, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 2.3 An application to set aside a witness summons referred to in paragraph 2.1 will be heard:] (2) in the County Court by a District Judge.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 2.3 An application to set aside a witness summons referred to in paragraph 2.1 will be heard:] 2.4 Unless the court otherwise directs, the applicant must give at least 2 days’ notice to the party who issued the witness summons of the application, which will normally be dealt with at a hearing.

## Travelling expenses and compensation for loss of time

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Travelling expenses and compensation for loss of time] 3.1 When a witness is served with a witness summons they must be offered a sum to cover his travelling expenses to and from the court and compensation for their loss of time 5 .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Travelling expenses and compensation for loss of time] 3.2 If the witness summons is to be served by the court, the party issuing the summons must deposit with the court:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Travelling expenses and compensation for loss of time] (1) a sum sufficient to pay for the witness’s expenses in travelling to the court and in returning to his home or place of work, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Travelling expenses and compensation for loss of time] (2) a sum in respect of the period during which earnings or benefit are lost, or such lesser sum as it may be proved that the witness will lose as a result of his attendance at court in answer to the witness summons.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Travelling expenses and compensation for loss of time] 3.3 The sum referred to in 3.2(2) is to be based on the sums payable to witnesses attending the Crown Court 6 .

## 3.4 Where the party issuing the witness summons wishes to serve it they must

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 3.4 Where the party issuing the witness summons wishes to serve it they must] (1) notify the court in writing that they wish to do so, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 3.4 Where the party issuing the witness summons wishes to serve it they must] (2) at the time of service offer the witness the sums mentioned in paragraph 3.2 above.

## DEPOSITIONS

## To be taken in England and Wales for use as evidence in proceedings in courts in England and Wales

## 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (1) a judge,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (2) an examiner of the court, or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (3) such other person as the court may appoint 8 .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] 4.2 The party who obtains an order for the examination of a deponent before an examiner of the court must:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (1) apply to the Foreign Process Section at the Royal Courts of Justice for the allocation of an examiner; alternatively engage a person who satisfies the criteria in CPR 34.8 (3) (a) or (c);

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (2) when allocated or engaged, provide the examiner with copies of all documents in the proceedings necessary to inform the examiner of the issues; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (3) pay the deponent a sum to cover their travelling expenses to and from the examination and compensation for their loss of time

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] 4.3 In ensuring that the deponent’s evidence is recorded in full, the court or the examiner may permit it to be recorded by audio or video, but the deposition 12 must always be recorded in writing by them or by a competent shorthand writer or stenographer.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] 4.4 If the deposition is not recorded word for word, it must contain, as nearly as may be, the statement of the deponent; the examiner may record word for word any particular questions and answers which appear to them to have special importance.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] 4.5 If a deponent objects to answering any question or where any objection is taken to any question, the examiner must:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (1) record in the deposition or a document attached to it –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (a) the question,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (b) the nature of and grounds for the objection, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (c) any answer given, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] (2) give their opinion as to the validity of the objection and must record it in the deposition or a document attached to it.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1 A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined on oath before:] The court will decide as to the validity of the objection and any question of costs arising from it.

## 4.6 Documents and exhibits must:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.6 Documents and exhibits must:] (1) have an identifying number or letter marked on them by the examiner, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.6 Documents and exhibits must:] (2) be preserved by the party or their legal representative 13 who obtained the order for the examination, or as the court or the examiner may direct.

## 4.7 The examiner may put any question to the deponent as to:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.7 The examiner may put any question to the deponent as to:] (1) the meaning of any of their answers, or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.7 The examiner may put any question to the deponent as to:] (2) any matter arising in the course of the examination.

## 4.8 Where a deponent:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] (1) fails to attend the examination, or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] (2) refuses to:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] (a) be sworn, or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] (b) answer any lawful question, or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] (c) produce any document,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] the examiner will sign a certificate 14 of such failure or refusal and may include in their certificate any comment as to the conduct of the deponent or of any person attending the examination.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] 4.9 The party who obtained the order for the examination must file the certificate with the court and may apply for an order that the deponent attend for examination or as may be 15 . The application may be made without notice 16 .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] 4.10 The court will make such order on the application as it thinks fit including an order for the deponent to pay any costs resulting from their failure or refusal 17 .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.8 Where a deponent:] 4.11 A deponent who wilfully refuses to obey an order made against them under Part 34 may be proceeded against for contempt of court.

## 4.12 A deposition must:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.12 A deposition must:] (1) be signed by the examiner,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.12 A deposition must:] (2) have any amendments to it initialled by the examiner and the deponent,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.12 A deposition must:] (3) be endorsed by the examiner with –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.12 A deposition must:] (a) a statement of the time occupied by the examination, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.12 A deposition must:] (b) a record of any refusal by the deponent to sign the deposition and of their reasons for not doing so, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.12 A deposition must:] (4) be sent by the examiner to the court where the proceedings are taking place for filing on the court file.

## 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.1 Where a party wishes to take a deposition from a person outside the jurisdiction, the High Court may order the issue of a letter of request to the judicial authorities of the country in which the proposed deponent is 18 .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.2 An application for an order referred to in paragraph 5.1 should be made by application notice in accordance with Part 23.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.3 The documents which a party applying for an order for the issue of a letter of request must file with their application notice are set out in rule 34.13(6). They are as follows:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] (1) a draft letter of request in the form set out in Annex A to this practice direction,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] (2) a statement of the issues relevant to the proceedings,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] (3) a list of questions or the subject matter of questions to be put to the proposed deponent,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] (4) a translation of the documents in (1), (2) and (3) above, unless the proposed deponent is in a country of which English is an official language, and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] (5) an undertaking to be responsible for the expenses of the Secretary of State (see Form PF78: Solicitor’s Undertaking as to Expenses (rule 34.13(6)(b)) – GOV.UK (www.gov.uk)

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] In addition to the documents listed above the party applying for the order must file a draft order.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.4 The above documents should be filed with the Foreign Process Section of the Royal Courts of Justice..

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.5 The application will be dealt with by the Senior Master of the King’s Bench Division of the High Court who will, if appropriate, sign the letter of request.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.6 Attention is drawn to the provisions of rule 23.10 (application to vary or discharge an order made without notice).

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.7 If parties are in doubt as to whether a translation under paragraph 5.3(4) above is required, they should seek guidance from the Foreign Process Section.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.8 A special examiner appointed under rule 34.13(4) may be the British Consul or the Consul-General or his deputy in the country where the evidence is to be taken if:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] (1) there is in respect of that country a Civil Procedure Convention providing for the taking of evidence in that country for the assistance of proceedings in the High Court or other court in this country, or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] (2) with the consent of the Secretary of State.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 5.9 The provisions of paragraphs 4.1 to 4.12 above apply to the depositions referred to in this paragraph.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.13 Rule 34.14 deals with the fees and expenses of an examiner.] 6.1 Section II of Part 34 relating to obtaining evidence for foreign courts applies to letters of request and should be read in conjunction with this part of the practice direction.

## 6.2 The Evidence (Proceedings in Other Jurisdictions) Act 1975 applies to these depositions.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.2 The Evidence (Proceedings in Other Jurisdictions) Act 1975 applies to these depositions.] 6.3 An application under rule 34.17 must be filed with the Foreign Process Section at the Royal Courts of Justice and include or exhibit—

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.2 The Evidence (Proceedings in Other Jurisdictions) Act 1975 applies to these depositions.] (1) a statement of the issues relevant to the proceedings;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.2 The Evidence (Proceedings in Other Jurisdictions) Act 1975 applies to these depositions.] (2) a list of questions or the subject matter of questions to be put to the proposed deponent;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.2 The Evidence (Proceedings in Other Jurisdictions) Act 1975 applies to these depositions.] (3) a translation of the documents in (1) and (2) into English, if necessary; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.2 The Evidence (Proceedings in Other Jurisdictions) Act 1975 applies to these depositions.] (4) where the application is made by an application notice under Part 23 in accordance with rule 34.17(2)(a), a draft order.”

## 6.4

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] (1) The Senior Master will send to the Treasury Solicitor any request –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] (a) forwarded by the Secretary of State with a recommendation that effect should be given to the request without requiring an application to be made; or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] (b) received by him in pursuance of a Civil Procedure Convention providing for the taking of evidence of any person in England and Wales to assist a court or tribunal in a foreign country where no person is named in the document as the applicant.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] (2) In relation to such a request, the Treasury Solicitor may, with the consent of the Treasury –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] (a) apply for an order under the 1975 Act; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] (b) take such other steps as are necessary to give effect to the request.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] 6.5 The order for the deponent to attend and be examined together with the evidence upon which the order was made must be served on the deponent.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] 6.6 Attention is drawn to the provisions of rule 23.10 (application to vary or discharge an order made without notice).

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] 6.7 Arrangements for the examination to take place at a specified time and place before an examiner of the court or such other person as the court may appoint shall be made by the applicant for the order and approved by the Senior Master.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] 6.8 The provisions of paragraph 4.2 to 4.12 apply to the depositions referred to in this paragraph, except that the examiner must send the deposition to the Senior Master.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6.4] (For further information about evidence see Part 32 and Practice Direction 32.)

## Annex A Draft Letter of Request (where the Taking of Evidence Regulation does not apply)

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Annex A Draft Letter of Request (where the Taking of Evidence Regulation does not apply)] To the Competent Judicial Authority of  [name of court] in [country]

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Annex A Draft Letter of Request (where the Taking of Evidence Regulation does not apply)] I [name] Senior Master of the King’s Bench Division of the Senior Courts of England and Wales respectfully request the assistance of your court with regard to the following matters.

## 1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1] A claim is now pending in the            Division of the High Court of Justice in England and Wales entitled as follows [set out full title and claim number] in which [name] of [address] is the claimant and [name] of [address] is the defendant.

## 2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 2] The names and addresses of the representatives or agents of [set out names and addresses of representatives of the parties].

## 3

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 3] The claim by the claimant is for:-

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 3] (a) [set out the nature of the claim]

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 3] (b) [the relief sought, and]

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 3] (c) [a summary of the facts.]

## 4

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4] It is necessary for the purposes of justice and for the due determination of the matters in dispute between the parties that you cause the following witnesses, who are resident within your jurisdiction, to be examined. The names and addresses of the witnesses are as follows:

## 5

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 5] The witnesses should be examined on oath or if that is not possible within your laws or is impossible of performance by reason of the internal practice and procedure of your court or by reason of practical difficulties, they should be examined in accordance with whatever procedure your laws provide for in these matters.

## 6

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6] Either/

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6] The witnesses should be examined in accordance with the list of questions annexed hereto.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6] Or/

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6] The witnesses should be examined regarding [set out full details of evidence sought]

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 6] N.B. Where the witness is required to produce documents, these should be clearly identified.

## 7

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 7] I would ask that you cause me, or the agents of the parties (if appointed), to be informed of the date and place where the examination is to take place.

## 8

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] Finally, I request that you will cause the evidence of the said witnesses to be reduced into writing and all documents produced on such examinations to be duly marked for identification and that you will further be pleased to authenticate such examinations by the seal of your court or in such other way as is in accordance with your procedure and return the written evidence and documents produced to me addressed as follows:

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] Senior Master of the King’s Bench Division

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] Royal Courts of Justice

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] Strand

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] London WC2A 2LL

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] England

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] Dated

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] Signed

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 8] Senior Master of the King’s Bench Division
